title: Myth flip — the 28-day cycle your app made up
caption:
Myth: your cycle is 28 days. Across 600,000 real cycles, only ~13% were (npj Digital Medicine, 2019). And phase-based training advice? Low-quality evidence (Sports Medicine, 2020).
Which myth next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#cyclesyncing #womenshealth #periodtracking #hormonehealth #cycletracking

scenes.text: My app swears I'm ovulating today. My body says *otherwise*.

scenes.text: Nandini is 36. Her planner promised a *high energy* week; she could barely finish the school run.
phrases: She could barely finish the school run.
So she decided the broken thing was her.

scenes.text: In 600,000 tracked cycles, only *13%* actually ran 28 days. The default was never the norm.
The phase-based training rules? Reviewers graded the evidence *low* and said go by your own data.
phrases: So she looked up the 'train by your phase' rules.
Evidence graded low. Their advice: go individual, not by chart.

scenes.text: Write down two things: your cycle day, and how tired you actually felt at *4pm*.
phrases: Log cycle day + your 4pm energy for 3 months.
Move ~150 minutes a week, whenever you can (WHO).
Eat iron-rich food with something citrusy — it absorbs better (NIH ODS).
